subject: First Trust Bank — control evidence, RTO/RPO clarifications and DR runbook request
messages:
From: Elena Morales <procurement@firsttrustbank.com>

Cc: Tom Reynolds <audit@firsttrustbank.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Control evidence and restoration testing schedule

Neha,

Thanks for continuing to engage on our resilience and audit requirements. As part of First Trust Bank's vendor control review (FFIEC-aligned), we need a few clarifications and a tentative timeline for evidence delivery:

- Control mapping: a crosswalk that maps Redwood controls to FFIEC CAT/ID/BCP control categories (high level is fine, a one-pager + appendix expected).
- Recovery objectives: explicit RTO/RPO for model serving and stateful services (KV cache, prefix caches, client session rehydration).
- DR failover runbook: steps for an active-region outage and cold failover to an alternate region; include estimated cutover time and manual vs automated steps.
- Test evidence: most recent DR exercise report and associated runbook changes (last 12 months).
- Encryption/KMS: diagram and attestation describing key custody, rotation cadence, and HSM/KMS integrations for private deployments.
- Logs and audit: retention windows for audit logs, access control evidence (who can access, role lists).

Can you share the expected delivery date for a preliminary package (control mapping + SOC2 summary + DR runbook) and whether you have slots for a 60-minute deep-dive call next week (Dec 7-9)? We're aiming to complete vendor analysis by Dec 17.

If anything is sensitive, mark it and we'll request an NDA or secure transfer method.

Best,
Elena Morales
Senior Procurement Manager | First Trust Bank
procurement@firsttrustbank.com

Elena — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the initial package and propose follow-up slots.

Summary of what we'll deliver by EOD Dec 8 (preliminary):
- "Control crosswalk (FFIEC mapping)" — high-level crosswalk + control owner mapping (PDF).
- "SOC2-Summary-Redwood-2026.pdf" — SOC 2 scope, in-scope services, and a summary of relevant controls (redacted where required).
- "DR_runbook_excerpt.txt" — focused runbook extract describing RTO/RPO statements and failover steps for model serving.
- "Redwood_RiskMatrix_FirstTrust_v1.xlsx" — gap tracker for items that may need remediation commitment.

High-level answers to some of your bullets:
- Recovery objectives: For our hosted API service tier, typical RTO for request continuity is 15-30 minutes for automated region failover; cold failover to a warmed standby region is documented at ~2-4 hours depending on customer data residency/configuration. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can set contractual RTOs; we provide the playbook and automation hooks.
- Caching/state: KV caches are ephemeral and designed for warm recovery; we persist enough metadata to rehydrate sessions in under 10 minutes in the warm-standby path. For customers requiring strict RPO, we offer snapshotting modes and export hooks.
- KMS/keys: We support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and bring-your-own-key for Dedicated; our hosted service uses cloud KMS with rotation and access logs.
- Logs: Audit logs retained 13 months by default for hosted; longer retention available as an add-on.

Next steps:
1) I'll upload the preliminary package to a secure Drive folder and share a link (see related_links).
2) Ben (Sales) — can you and Marissa run through the suggested remediation commitments? We may want to offer specific contractual language for RTO items.
3) Elena/Tom — are you available for a 60-minute deep dive on Dec 8 at 10:00 AM EST? If not, suggest alternate times.

We'll mark sensitive docs and, if needed, execute an NDA before transferring full artifacts.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security & Trust Programs | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

- DR runbook excerpt (TXT/PDF) — automated failover sequence, manual rollback steps, estimated cutover times (automated 15-30m; manual cold failover 2-4h).

Please confirm if Dec 11 final is acceptable or if you need select items earlier. Happy to take the deep-dive on Dec 8 if that still works.
